basic_identification.full_title: Electric Traction Lifts — Part 3: Safety Rules — Section 1: Passenger and Goods Lifts (विद्युत कर्षी लिफ्ट — भाग 3: सुरक्षा नियम — अनुभाग 1: यात्री और माल लिफ्ट)
basic_identification.sector_category: Electrotechnical / Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks (approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council and finalized by the Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Sectional Committee, ETD 25, formerly ETDC 25, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the essential safety rules, mechanical and structural parameters, electrical protection, clearances, and testing procedures for the design and construction of electric traction passenger and goods lifts to safeguard users, maintenance mechanics, and emergency rescue teams.

version_status_and_amendments.supersedes: IS 4666 : 1980 (Specification for electric passenger and goods lifts)
version_status_and_amendments.superseded_by: IS 17900 (Part 1 & Part 2) : 2024 / ISO 8100-1 & 2 (Official mandatory enforcement took effect on December 22, 2025, completely withdrawing and replacing the IS 14665 series for all new building installations in India)

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice for General Steel Construction
allied_standards.relevance: The master structural steel code in India, regulating support steelwork, overhead structural channels, guide rail mounting brackets, and machine foundation beams.

allied_standards.title: Openwell Submersible Pumpsets — Specification
allied_standards.relevance: Submersible drainage pumps are mandatory in elevator pits to prevent accumulation of groundwater which can corrupt electrical safety switches and corrode structural buffers.

allied_standards.title: Insulating Varnishes Containing Solvents — Specification
allied_standards.relevance: Traction motors used in elevator sheave gear structures are insulated with varnishes conforming to IS 10026 to ensure reliable starting torque and high dielectric stability.

allied_standards.title: Methods of Test for Determination of Flammability of Solid Electrical Insulating Materials when Exposed to an Igniting Source: Part 2 Vertical Specimen Method
allied_standards.relevance: Plastic lenses, wire trunking, terminal blocks, and panel covers inside the lift car and controller must be self-extinguishing (FV0) to prevent toxic smoke or fire spread.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice on Occupational Safety and Health Audit
allied_standards.relevance: Enforces strict safety audits during elevator shaft installation and maintenance, ensuring that technicians use personal fall-arrest systems, safety nets, and LOTO (lock-out/tag-out) protocols.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Safety & Code of Practice (Electrotechnical Department / Lifts)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Mandatory Certification under various State Lift Acts & Rules (e.g., Delhi Lift Rules, Maharashtra Lift Act). Licences to operate elevators are granted by State Lift Inspectors only upon verifying compliance with the safety rules of IS 14665, with key certified components carrying the physical ISI mark.

requirements.detail: Observed or calculated final test values, maximum net car areas, clearances, and emergency battery back-up capacities must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

Strict limits are set on the inside car area relative to rated loads to prevent hazardous overcrowding. Car dimensions are measured panel-to-panel at a height of 1 m from the finished floor (e.g. 4 passengers / 272 kg requires a net area of 0.68 to 0.77 sq m).

Under Amendment No. 1, every passenger lift must carry an automatic overload sensor. If loaded to 110% of capacity or more, the car must remain stationary with doors fully open, and activate an audio-visual alarm.

Under Amendment No. 1, all passenger lifts must have a battery-operated ARD to automatically move the car to the nearest landing during power cuts. It must open doors and activate an audio-visual trapped passenger indicator. Capacity must sustain at least 3 rescue cycles.

No lift can start or run unless all landing doors are closed and mechanically locked. Positive electromechanical interlocks must physically confirm lock engagement before the safety circuit is completed.
The lift car must be equipped with natural ventilation openings or fans and emergency battery back-up lighting to operate during power failures to prevent occupant panic.

keywords: Rated load vs net car area

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 14665 (Part 3/Sec 1) : 2000 (Reaffirmed 2020) is the primary national Indian Standard safety code governing the construction, installation, and operation of electric traction passenger and goods elevators. Maintained under the Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks committee (ETD 25), the standard establishes strict mechanical and electrical rules—such as electro-mechanical door interlocks, car clearances, and strict capacity-to-area limits (preventing overcrowding). Under active amendments, elevators must be equipped with automatic overload cut-outs (preventing movement at 110% capacity with doors open) and battery-powered Automatic Rescue Devices (ARD) that automatically move a trapped elevator car to the nearest landing during power cuts. To align with modern global standards, the standard was officially withdrawn on December 22, 2025, and superseded by the unified, performance-based code IS 17900:2025 for all new elevator installations, remaining active only as the legal inspection reference for pre-existing in-service elevators.
